$comment: What each web release changed, for the person deciding whether to press Update in the desktop app (and anyone reading release notes). Newest first; one entry per merged pull request that ships to production, keyed by its number. Plain words only: no file paths, component names or migration numbers. A release with no entry here still ships with notes: /api/web-release falls back to the pull request's title.

releases.headline: Match predictions now come from the robots on the field
changes: Each robot is rated by what it has actually scored at this event, plus what your scouts saw it do, so Home predicts your next match even where no outside ratings exist
Predicted scores are about twice as close to the real result: measured on real matches, the typical miss fell from 86 points to about 40
Win chances and the ± around each score now fit how high your game scores, instead of calling almost every match 98% to 2%
Home shows the win chance for your next match before anyone presses Predict this match

releases.headline: Five places to find everything: Home, Competition, Team, Build and Business
changes: The sidebar on a computer and the bar at the bottom of your phone are now the same five places, in the same order; the menu button, the slide-out menu and More are gone
Each place shows its sections in a row under the title, so Scout, Match plan, Pick list and the rest are one tap away
Search is now Search or ask: type a question and choose Ask AI, or just press Enter, and the assistant picks it up
On your phone, your pinned tools sit at the top of search; on a computer they stay under the five places in the sidebar
Settings, Help and Admin moved into the account menu at the top right

releases.headline: Your next match is always on Home, with Predict this match
changes: During an event, Home shows your next match at the top: bumper colour, who's with and against you, the countdown, and what comes after
Predict this match re-scores it from the latest data and writes the match plan for the whole team; it can take up to 5 minutes
The score estimate on Home now uses each robot's ratings at this event, so it shows up even before season ratings are loaded

releases.headline: Shop steps with drawing QR codes, a shop kiosk, and buying by vendor
changes: Every part on the Manufacturing board has its own page: the steps to make it in order, its drawing, and one button for the next step
Print a part's QR label onto its drawing; scanning it opens the steps on any phone
A shop kiosk shows every part on the floor and the step it's on, with big Start and Done buttons and a who's-working picker
Orders groups approved requests one cart per vendor; check a cart out with what you actually paid, including shipping and tax
The budget now counts what an order actually cost once it's bought, and each request shows paid next to expected

releases.headline: Skill trees, a scout points game, and phone check-in at the door
changes: Training opens on skill trees: Safety, Manufacturing, Design and CAD, Electrical, Programming, Drive team, Scouting, Pit crew and Leadership, each skill unlocking after the one before it, with Safety opening the rest
Mentors sign off a skill for a whole training session at once, and see the team's progress in each tree at a glance
Scout home has a points board: 10 a match report, 15 a pit visit, +5 for covering your own assignment, with streaks
Hours has a door check-in screen: members scan its QR code with their phone to check in and out, and it changes every minute so it only works at the door
A received order that wasn't linked to an inventory item now adds itself to inventory

releases.headline: No more warning boxes when a page is simply showing its saved copy
changes: When a page can't refresh but has its last copy on your device, it says so in a quiet grey line instead of an amber warning
Offline, that line no longer repeats what the offline banner already says
Real problems, like a page with nothing saved, still show as a warning

releases.headline: Event pages open from this device first
changes: Event Day, My Day and the schedule are kept saved on your phone or laptop and refreshed quietly every 30 minutes, so they open instantly in a crowded venue
Save event day on this phone now also saves Strategy and the pre-match briefing
The quiet refresh never runs offline or on a data-saver connection

releases.headline: A match plan that writes itself before each match
changes: The pre-match briefing opens with a match plan: our odds, how to raise them, what each opponent will most likely do and how, each partner's job, and auto, teleop and endgame
It is written automatically when you open the match and the plan is out of date, using every match and scouting report since the last one
Write a new plan rewrites it on demand, and everyone on the team sees the newest plan within a minute
With AI connected it is written by your team's model (Claude Haiku 5.5 by default); without AI, Vantage writes it from the same numbers
Turn automatic plans off in Settings › Appearance › Match day

releases.headline: Predictions use ten seasons of history, fairly compared
changes: Win chances weigh up to ten seasons, this season first and each earlier one counting about half as much
A past game's numbers are compared on this season's scale, since every game scores differently
A long past season can no longer outweigh this season's first event
Strategy shows each team's history in words: top 10% for years running, climbing, or slipping
Platform admins can load ten past seasons of team ratings in one step
Sign-in and account recovery buttons now match the app's blue

releases.headline: Local AI in the desktop app (experimental)
changes: The desktop app can answer your AI requests with a model running on your own computer in LM Studio
It checks for 16 GB of memory and 15 GB of free disk first, and pairs to your account so it only receives your own requests
Team → Personal AI connection shows the computer's local model, and its Everything setting extends it to every AI feature
When the local model is off, your team's normal AI answers as before

releases.headline: Fewer buttons, and errors only when something failed
changes: CAD starts with one step, Link an Onshape document; the assistant appears once a document is linked
Pick list is its own menu item, with Ranking and Discussion tabs, one Add to… menu per team and Save beside the list
Code's repo scan keeps its settings in one Scan settings group instead of price cards and badges
Deleting a lesson draft, an attendance event or a scouting report is in a More menu and asks first
Settings pages have one way back, the Calendar dialog has labels and a Cancel button, and Home appears once in the sidebar
Looking up a team Vantage hasn't synced shows its public profile instead of a dead end
Older iPads no longer see Couldn't reach Vantage when the connection is fine
Setup prompts are calm notes, not warnings, and Strategy no longer shows a fake Choose your team screen when the server hiccups
Ask AI opens ready to type when AI already works for your team
The Appearance page says what your device is set to, and the logo stays visible in dark mode

releases.headline: Faster first load
changes: Home asks the server for its board once instead of twice when it opens
Home shows its outline the moment you tap it, before anything else arrives
Scouting opens with less to download: team profiles, data checks and QR handoff load when you open those tabs
Every app page skips about 190 KB of website styling it never used
The data-connection banner is checked once every 30 seconds instead of on every page load
The account recovery form keeps both name boxes inside the card

releases.headline: An easier scouting form builder
changes: Answer types are grouped (Count, Choose, Rate, Text, Field and time) with plain descriptions
Required is right next to each question instead of under More
The preview shows the quick tiles scouts actually use, with the full form one tap away
An option can contain a comma without splitting in two
Assigning or swapping a scout can be undone straight away
A No on a yes/no tile now looks like an answer

releases.headline: Plain words everywhere
changes: Messages no longer mention database updates or internal numbers; they say when something is not available yet
Failure log, form versions, tablet sharing and other names replace technical terms
Status badges read like words (In progress, Final) instead of stored codes
Labels are written in normal case instead of capitals, which screen readers spell out

releases.headline: The desktop app now tells you when Vantage updates, and what changed
changes: When a new version of Vantage is live, the desktop app asks before switching to it and lists what changed
It never interrupts a scouting or match screen you're looking at; Later asks again in two hours

releases.headline: Calmer pages: one main button each, tabs instead of long scrolls
changes: Code review has three tabs (Review, Repo scan, Pull requests) and one main button on each
Kickoff is split into Overview, Scoring, Priorities, Rules and Next season
Pick list, People and CAD lost their repeated links, tiles and duplicate buttons
Home has one main action, Up next, and you can bring back empty cards with one tap

releases.headline: One menu, one search, one name for each place
changes: The sidebar and the phone menu list the same four workspaces
Search is in one place on every screen size
The phone tab bar ends in More; Pit TV and Assignments open straight away
Admin's sections are tabs across the top instead of a second column

releases.headline: Email sign-in codes work again
changes: Signing in with a code sent to your email had stopped working; it works again
Feedback, problem reports and support tickets now reach the Vantage team's inbox

releases.headline: Clearer buttons, and delete buttons that stay out of the way
changes: Delete, remove and disconnect buttons are red, sit apart from the others and ask first
The scouting Save button no longer turns grey with instructions on it; a failed save takes you to the question to fix
Buttons have one size and shape across the app
